composer.story_text:
Her confirmation was precise and deliberately small. "This is the Hanezawa residence." She let the answer stand at that—no follow-on, no warmth, no suggestion that she recognized the speaker or expected him. What had been asked for was the address; she would give nothing beyond it.

The speaker had not offered a name. That was not evidence against him; it was simply an empty field in an exchange she had no reason to advance. "Your name," she said, "and the purpose of your visit." Her tone stayed even and administrative, as though she were completing a form rather than deciding whether to trust a stranger.

Then she fell quiet, leaving the next words to the speaker. A name, a purpose, or a refusal—any of those would tell her more than silence ever would. Until one came, the threshold would remain unresolved, and she would not cross it with assumptions.
